# Translator {#sec-translator}

The translator is found in `backend/core/translator/`. It changes any transpiled
circuit into a sequence of native ion gates. Only `gpi`, `gpi2`, `virtual_z` and
**one** entangler, either `ms` or `zz`, appear in the result. The two entanglers
are never mixed.

Three files are used.

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `translator.py` | The abstract base class and the provider subclasses. |
| `rules.py` | The translation table, one rule per gate. |
| `normalize.py` | The entangling angle is reduced to the range [0, 0.25] turns. |

The opposite direction, rebuilding a Qiskit circuit from a native circuit, is not
part of the translator. It lives in its own module, described on the
[`to_qiskit` page](to-qiskit.qmd).

## The translator classes {.unnumbered}

One class exists per provider. All the classes share the same translation rule.
The only difference is the target entangler, which is taken from `BackendInfo`.

| Class | Provider |
| --- | --- |
| `IonQTranslator` | `"ionq"` |
| `IBMTranslator` | `"ibm"` |
| `AWSTranslator` | `"aws"` |
| `LocalTranslator` | `"local"` |
| `GenericTranslator` | `"unknown"` |

### `Translator` (abstract base class) {.unnumbered}

| Member | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `__init__(self, info)` | method | The `BackendInfo` is stored. It is used for the entangler and the profile. |
| `translate(self, transpiled)` | abstract method | A `TranspiledCircuit` is received, and a `NativeCircuit` is returned. |
| `_translate(self, transpiled)` | method | The shared implementation. It is called by every subclass. |

### `create(info)` {.unnumbered}

The correct subclass is built from the provider of the backend.

**Parameter**

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `info` | `BackendInfo` | The provider field selects the subclass. |

**Returns** a `Translator` of the matching subclass.

## The translation rules {.unnumbered}

The rules are given in `rules.py`. The temporal order is the list order: the
leftmost operation is applied first. All the identities are exact up to a global
phase, and a global phase does not change a Bloch vector.

| Source gate | Translation |
| --- | --- |
| `x` | `gpi(0)` |
| `y` | `gpi(π/2)` |
| `sx`, `sxdg` | `gpi2(0)`, `gpi2(π)` |
| `rz(λ)`, `p(λ)`, `u1(λ)` | `virtual_z(λ)` |
| `z`, `s`, `sdg`, `t`, `tdg` | `virtual_z` with `π`, `π/2`, `-π/2`, `π/4`, `-π/4` |
| `h` | `virtual_z(π)`, `gpi2(π/2)` |
| `cz(a,b)` | a `zz` operation, or the equivalent MS form, followed by `virtual_z(-π/2)` on both qubits |
| `cx(c,t)` with the MS entangler | `gpi2(c,π/2)`, `ms(c,t)`, `gpi2(c,π)`, `gpi2(t,π)`, `gpi2(c,-π/2)` |
| `cx(c,t)` with the ZZ entangler | `h(t)`, `cz(c,t)`, `h(t)` |
| `rzz(θ)` | `zz(θ / 2π)`, then normalized |
| an IonQ native gate | taken directly, with the phases changed from turns to radians |
| `id`, `barrier`, `delay`, a final `measure` | ignored |
| any other one-qubit gate | decomposed with the Euler decomposition, then translated |
| any other two-qubit gate | decomposed onto `cz`, then translated |
| a gate of three or more qubits | expanded through its definition, then translated |
| a mid-circuit `measure`, `reset`, or classical control | `UnsupportedOperationError` |

The one-qubit gates with a fixed angle (`x`, `y`, `sx`, `sxdg`, `z`, `s`, `sdg`,
`t`, `tdg`) are read from three small constant tables in `rules.py`, instead of
one branch each.

### `emit(ops, op, qubits, entangler, source_index=None)` {.unnumbered}

One Qiskit operation is translated, and the new native operations are appended
to the list `ops`.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ops` | list of `NativeOp` | The output list. New operations are appended to it. |
| `op` | Qiskit operation | The operation to translate. |
| `qubits` | tuple of int | The qubits the operation acts on. |
| `entangler` | `"ms"` or `"zz"` | The target entangler. |
| `source_index` | int or `None` | The index of the original instruction, copied onto each new operation. |

No value is returned. The list `ops` is changed.

### `emit_zz(ops, targets, angle, entangler, source_index=None)` {.unnumbered}

A `ZZ(angle)` operation is written, after the angle is normalized and after the
entangler is converted when necessary.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ops` | list of `NativeOp` | The output list. |
| `targets` | tuple of int | The two qubits. |
| `angle` | float | The angle in turns. It is normalized inside the function. |
| `entangler` | `"ms"` or `"zz"` | The target entangler. |
| `source_index` | int or `None` | The index of the original instruction. |

### `emit_ms(ops, targets, phases, angle, entangler, source_index=None)` {.unnumbered}

An `MS(phases, angle)` operation is written, in the same way.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ops` | list of `NativeOp` | The output list. |
| `targets` | tuple of int | The two qubits. |
| `phases` | tuple of two floats | The phases in radians. |
| `angle` | float | The angle in turns. |
| `entangler` | `"ms"` or `"zz"` | The target entangler. |
| `source_index` | int or `None` | The index of the original instruction. |

### `translate_circuit(circuit, layout, entangler)` {.unnumbered}

A whole Qiskit circuit is translated, and its qubits are compacted.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `circuit` | `QuantumCircuit` | The circuit to translate. |
| `layout` | tuple of int or `None` | The layout produced by the transpiler. |
| `entangler` | `"ms"` or `"zz"` | The target entangler. |

**Returns** a pair `(ops, num_qubits)`, where `ops` is a list of `NativeOp` and
`num_qubits` is the number of qubits after compaction.

### `translate_native_ops(native_ops, num_qubits, entangler)` {.unnumbered}

A raw IonQ native gate list is translated. This form is received when the native
API payload is read.

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `native_ops` | sequence of dict | Each dictionary has a `gate` key and a `target` or `targets` key. A `phase`, `phases` or `angle` key may also be present. Phases and angles are in turns. |
| `num_qubits` | int | The number of qubits. The targets are checked against it. |
| `entangler` | `"ms"` or `"zz"` | The target entangler. |

**Returns** a list of `NativeOp`.

**Raises** `UnsupportedOperationError` when an entry is malformed. The list comes
from a remote payload, so each entry is validated before it is used. These cases
are rejected, and the message gives the index of the entry:

- an entry that is not a dictionary;
- an unknown `gate`;
- a missing, non-numeric or out-of-range target, or a repeated target;
- a number of targets that does not fit the gate (one for `gpi` and `gpi2`, two
  for `ms` and `zz`);
- a missing or non-numeric `phase` (`gpi`, `gpi2`), a `phases` value that does
  not have two numbers (`ms`), or a non-numeric `angle`.

## The compaction of the qubits {.unnumbered}

A large backend, such as an IBM device with 156 qubits, is reduced to the qubits
that are used. The rules are the following.

- The user qubits are kept, in their original order. The order is read from the
  layout.
- A user qubit that is never used is still kept. It is a quiet ion in `|0⟩`.
- A physical qubit that is used only for routing is appended at the end.
- A physical qubit that is not touched is removed.

One limitation is accepted. A final permutation that is caused by routing is not
undone.

## The normalization of the angle {.unnumbered}

The file `normalize.py` reduces an entangling angle to the range [0, 0.25] turns.
The identities that are used are exact up to a global phase.

- One turn is subtracted or added when the angle is outside the range. This is a
  global phase, so it is free.
- Half a turn is subtracted when the absolute value is larger than 0.25. A
  conjugation is added to keep the operation correct.
- A negative angle is made positive by a conjugation on the first qubit.

### `normalize_zz(targets, angle)` {.unnumbered}

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `targets` | tuple of int | The two qubits. |
| `angle` | float | The angle in turns. |

**Returns** a list of `NativeOp`. When the angle is zero, an empty list is
returned and nothing is emitted.

### `normalize_ms(targets, phases, angle)` {.unnumbered}

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `targets` | tuple of int | The two qubits. |
| `phases` | tuple of two floats | The phases in radians. |
| `angle` | float | The angle in turns. |

**Returns** a list of `NativeOp`.

## A note on global phases {.unnumbered}

Some of the identities differ from the original gate by a global phase, for
example a factor of `-1` or `-i`. A global phase has no physical meaning, and it
does not change any Bloch vector. The tests therefore use an equivalence check
that ignores the global phase.
